blocks.title: Vulnerability Identification Methods exam shortcuts
items: Need broad automated weakness discovery → VULNERABILITY SCAN
Use scanners to identify known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
Example: An authenticated scan checks missing patches on servers.
Need to inspect code without running it → STATIC ANALYSIS
SAST finds issues in source or compiled code.
Example: A scanner detects unsafe functions during CI.
Need to test the live application → DYNAMIC ANALYSIS
DAST interacts with the running application.
Example: A scanner probes a web app for runtime vulnerabilities.
Need to test whether a weakness is truly exploitable → PENETRATION TEST
Example: An authorized tester gains access through a vulnerable service.
Researcher needs official reporting path → RESPONSIBLE DISCLOSURE
Use a defined channel to report findings safely.
Example: A company publishes a vulnerability disclosure policy.
Valid findings earn money → BUG BOUNTY
A bounty program rewards accepted vulnerability reports.
Example: A researcher receives payment for a confirmed flaw.
blocks.example: Focus on which stage of the vulnerability-management lifecycle the scenario is describing.

questions.q: A security team wants an automated method to identify known vulnerabilities and missing patches across servers. Which method is best?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability scanning is designed for broad automated identification of known weaknesses.

questions.q: A development team wants to find coding flaws without executing the application. Which technique is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Static analysis inspects source or compiled code without running the application.

questions.q: A tester assesses a running web application for security flaws. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Dynamic analysis tests the application during execution.

questions.q: A security tool alerts when a project uses a software library with a newly disclosed vulnerability. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Package monitoring tracks software dependencies and known vulnerable versions.

questions.q: A security analyst uses public advisories, search engines, and public repositories to research threats. Which source is this?
An organization pays for a commercial threat intelligence service. Which category is this?
questions.explanation: Commercial or private intelligence is proprietary or third-party intelligence.

questions.q: An industry group shares threat information among member companies. Which source is this?
questions.explanation: Information-sharing organizations distribute threat intelligence among participating members.

questions.q: An analyst searches for stolen credentials and leaked company data in hidden online forums. Which source is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Dark web monitoring may reveal stolen credentials, leaked data, or attacker discussions.

questions.q: An authorized tester actively exploits a weakness to determine whether it can lead to system compromise. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Penetration testing actively attempts exploitation to validate real-world impact.

questions.q: A company publishes a formal process for security researchers to report vulnerabilities safely. What is this?
questions.explanation: Responsible disclosure provides a defined reporting path for researchers.

questions.q: A company pays researchers for valid vulnerabilities found within a defined scope. Which program is this?
questions.explanation: Bug bounty programs reward accepted vulnerability findings.

questions.q: A formal review checks systems and procedures against required security controls. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: An audit reviews controls and processes against requirements or standards.
